user_approval_text:
Approved: V4.2 = V4.1 (SHA-256 e7735ae9…) plus the changes below. Produce the V4.2 JSON and verify that its diff from V4.1 is limited to:

version metadata;
the converter and its implementation bindings;
the GPU-owner allowance.

Record the V4.2 SHA-256 with this text. This is explicit approval. Proceed through steps 3–5 without further confirmation unless a stop condition is met.

Output converter.
Route every JSON write in the V4 audit path through one converter. This covers collection, branching, articulated clearance, filter, both references, panel and memo inputs.
The converter maps NumPy booleans, integers and floats to native Python values via .item(), and arrays via .tolist(). It leaves all other types unchanged.
Every written file is read back and compared with the in-memory values. Any mismatch is a stop.
During the pre-launch check only, further failures of this same kind (NumPy scalar or array serialisation) are pre-authorised for the converter, each logged. Any other defect stops for disposition, as does any writer failure during the Phase 2 run itself.
GPU-owner allowance: 72 hours, matching the wall cap. All other caps are unchanged.
End-to-end output check.
Run the complete V4.2 audit owner on the six qualified states, writing to a separate root.
Use retained traces if the owner can run from them. Otherwise, execute those six states' V4.2 assignments once, within caps.
Every output file must be written, read back and schema-validated.
The full downstream analysis must run on the written outputs: filter audit, both references, localisation panels, paired contrasts and panel assembly. Include the missing-value and unresolved paths.
These outputs are implementation checks only. They are not part of the Phase 2 panel, and no comparative results from them are retained as science.
Historical re-render check, as previously approved.
Phase 2 launch under V4.2.
